answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may post offers or vote, then slash that deposit when a fraud proof shows the identity double-spent a claim or colluded in a provable way. One person can still create many identities, but each one must tie up real capital, so a sybil swarm becomes expensive rather than free; the attacker also risks losing the stake. A dune of cheap accounts cannot simply mirror one trusted agent, while an honest haven remains open to newcomers who can afford the lock.
